correctness.rationale: The proof identifies the dyadic morphic blocks P_k and Q_k, proves that they differ only in the final bit, establishes by induction that S_k={2^j-1:0<=j<=k} attracts every prefix of length from 2^k through 2^(k+1)-1, and proves first failure at length 2^(k+1) using the unique occurrence of Q_k in P_kQ_k. The uniqueness argument excludes interior windows by one-count preservation under cyclic rotation. A standalone exhaustive checker independently replays the greedy definition on all prefixes through length 128 and verifies the dyadic identities through thirteen levels.

value.rationale: The greedy attractor was introduced as a natural computational surrogate for the difficult minimum-attractor problem, and the direct source proves only a general logarithmic bound. The exact period-doubling profile is a canonical structural benchmark: it shows that the logarithmic order is attained by the greedy rule even though the true optimum is constantly 2. This gives a sharp separation between the online greedy invariant and minimum attractors on a standard automatic word, rather than an arbitrary finite parameter increment.
